study type: Mixed-methods study (quantitative retrospective analysis and qualitative interviews)
cohort: The study included 2,794 patients (2018-2019) from three US hospitals desiring postpartum permanent contraception for quantitative analysis, and 67 patients and 54 obstetrician-gynecologists (2022-2023) for qualitative interviews.
finding: Delivery type significantly mediates the relationship between insurance type and postpartum permanent contraception fulfillment, with Medicaid patients having higher odds of vaginal delivery, which in turn was associated with reduced fulfillment.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was strongly associated with reduced permanent contraception fulfillment compared to cesarean delivery, as cesarean delivery often made permanent contraception easier due to provider discussions and logistical factors.
cross-section timing: Quantitative data from 2018-2019 and qualitative data from 2022-2023.
